result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers clearly reject the streak rule and propose anomaly-based relief that customers opt into. B is stronger on stopping a run: it adds a one-tap stop that must end before the bank cutoff and says plainly that sent funds can't be undone, and it lists unusually large hours as a trigger. A's cancel window doesn't say what becomes irreversible, and B slightly overstates support's 'hard to pull back' as 'can't be pulled back'. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers reject the streak rule and propose opt-in relief for routine runs that pass threshold checks, with full review when something changes. A does better on irreversibility: its hold must end before the bank cutoff, it tells customers plainly that sent funds can't be undone, and it makes the feature easy to leave. B frames the anomaly signal a little more sharply, but its cancel window never says what can't be reversed after sending. A slightly overstates Support by saying mistakes 'can't' be pulled back, when Support said 'hard to pull back'.
